newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania avg monthly inflation up at 3.8 pct in '96.
newsitem.headline: Romania avg monthly inflation up at 3.8 pct in '96.

text.p: Romania's average monthly inflation quickened to 3.8 percent last year from 2.1 in 1995 mainly due last July's increases in electricity and fuel prices, the National Statistics Board (CNS) said on Friday.

"After a period of relative stability in the first four months (of 1996), when the average monthly rate was 1.7 percent, monthly inflation rose, hitting three peaks in May, July and December," a CNS report showed.
Romania had a monthly inflation of 5.3 percent last May, following rises in the prices meat and milk -- which account for 18.2 percent of total individual monthly spending.
Last July, inflation soared to a monthly 7.5 percent after increases in bread, electricity, fuel and heating prices.

Under pressure from the World Bank to bring energy prices closer to international levels, Romania increased electricity and thermal power prices by 58 percent and the price of fuel by some 30 percent early last July.
Consumer price inflation quickened to 10.3 percent last December under seasonal price fluctuations and a weakened leu currency, which affected import prices, the report said.
Average monthly inflation in 1996 was 3.7 percent in the food sector, compared with 1.9 percent in 1995, and 4.0 percent in the non-food sector, up from a 1995 level of 2.0 percent, the report said.
Inflation in the services sector was at a monthly average of 3.6 percent in 1996, up from 2.9 percent the previous year.
Romania ended 1996 with 12-month inflation of 56.9 percent, double the previous year's 27.8 percent and triple a 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
The Fund last year suspended a $460 million loan accord on grounds that the former leftist government had missed targets and spent too much in an election year.
The new centrist coalition ruling Romania since last November's polls, is now discussing a reform package liable to unlock IMF money. The talks are expected to conclude next week.

No official forecast for 12-month inflation this year was issued so far, but local economists expect a rate of around 70 percent at the end of June after fuel price rises in January and energy price increases expected in the coming months.
